result.topic_en: Four results (numbered 6 to 9) on the Rogers–Ramanujan continued fraction: its relation to eta-quotients and Lambert series, modular equations of degree 5 and 25 expressed through it, and a reciprocity relation for its values at α and β with αβ = π².
result.transcription:
Add. Ms a 94 18 (105) (105)
(6) If $v = \frac{x^{1/5}}{1+} \frac{x}{1+} \frac{x^2}{1+} \frac{x^3}{1+} \frac{x^4}{1+} \cdots$
then $x\left(\frac{1}{v^5}+v^5\right) . \frac{(1-x^5)^5(1-x^{10})^5(1-x^{15})^5\cdots}{(1-x)(1-x^2)(1-x^3)\cdots}$
$= 1 + 6\sum_{n=1}^{n=\infty}\left(\frac{nx^n}{1-x^n} - \frac{5nx^{5n}}{1-x^{5n}}\right).$
(7). If $2u = 11 + \frac{1}{x}\cdot\left\{\frac{(1-x)(1-x^2)(1-x^3)\cdots}{(1-x^5)(1-x^{10})(1-x^{15})\cdots}\right\}^6$
and $2v = 1 + \frac{1}{x^{1/5}}\cdot\left\{\frac{(1-x^{1/5})(1-x^{2/5})(1-x^{3/5})\cdots}{(1-x)(1-x^2)(1-x^3)\cdots}\right\}$
then $\sqrt[5]{\sqrt{u^2+1}-u} = \sqrt{v^2+1}-v$
$= \frac{\sqrt[5]{x}}{1+}\frac{x}{1+}\frac{x^2}{1+}\frac{x^3}{1+}\frac{x^4}{1+}\cdots$
(8) If $2u = 11 + 125x.\left\{\frac{(1-x^5)(1-x^{10})(1-x^{15})\cdots}{(1-x)(1-x^2)(1-x^3)\cdots}\right\}^6$
and $2v = 1 + 5x.\left\{\frac{(1-x^{25})(1-x^{50})(1-x^{75})\cdots}{(1-x)(1-x^2)(1-x^3)\cdots}\right\}$
then, $\frac{\sqrt5}{1+\left(\frac{\sqrt5-1}{2}\right)\sqrt[5]{\sqrt{u^2+1}-u}} = \frac{\sqrt5}{1+\left(\frac{\sqrt5-1}{2}\right)\left(\sqrt{v^2+1}-v\right)}$
$= \frac{1+\sqrt5}{2} + \frac{x}{1+}\frac{x^5}{1+}\frac{x^{10}}{1+}\frac{x^{15}}{1+}\cdots$
(9) If $\alpha\beta = \pi^2$, then
$\left\{\left(\frac{\sqrt5+1}{2}\right)^5 + \left(\frac{e^{-2\alpha/5}}{1+}\frac{e^{-2\alpha}}{1+}\frac{e^{-4\alpha}}{1+}\cdots\right)^5\right\}$
$\times\left\{\left(\frac{\sqrt5+1}{2}\right)^5 + \left(\frac{e^{-2\beta/5}}{1+}\frac{e^{-2\beta}}{1+}\frac{e^{-4\beta}}{1+}\cdots\right)^5\right\}$
$= 5\sqrt5\cdot\left(\frac{\sqrt5+1}{2}\right)^5.$

methods.what: Identity relating v^{-5}+v^5 for the Rogers–Ramanujan continued fraction v to an eta-quotient and a Lambert series

Continued fraction (1+√5)/2 + x/(1+ x^5/(1+ ...)) expressed via eta-quotients of degree 5 and 25
Reciprocity (modular transformation) formula for the Rogers–Ramanujan continued fraction with αβ = π²

items.english: Result (6): if v is the Rogers–Ramanujan continued fraction, then the stated identity with the Lambert series holds (stated without proof).
Result (7): with u and v defined by the given products, the fifth root of √(u²+1)−u equals √(v²+1)−v, which equals the continued fraction (stated without proof).
Result (8): with u and v defined by the given products, the stated expressions equal the continued fraction (stated without proof).
Result (9): if αβ = π², the product of the two bracketed expressions equals 5√5((√5+1)/2)^5 (stated without proof).
